title: 2nd Mystery The Equality Of Few And Many Through The Mystery Of Luminosity And Obedience

questions.question: What is the main idea of the Second Mystery?
questions.answer: It explains that Allah’s power can deal with countless things as easily as one thing, so large and small numbers make no difference to Him.

questions.question: Which three qualities are named at the beginning as part of this mystery?
questions.answer: Brightness, clarity, and obedience.

questions.question: What example is used first to help explain this mystery?
questions.answer: The example of one sun showing its image and effects in many reflecting surfaces.

questions.question: In the example of the sun, what does one mirror show us?
questions.answer: It shows that a single source can appear in one place without losing anything.

questions.question: What do the many mirrors, shiny things, and drops help the reader understand?
questions.answer: They help the reader understand how one source can give the same effect to many places at once.

questions.question: According to the passage, does the sun’s reflection become harder when the number of mirrors increases?
questions.answer: No. The point is that many reflections can appear without making the act difficult.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw about big and small things from the sun example?
questions.answer: It says there is no real difference for Divine power between what is large and what is small.

questions.question: What second everyday example is given after the sun?
questions.answer: A single word being heard by one person and also by many people.

questions.question: What does the example of one word reaching many ears teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that one act can extend to many receivers without becoming difficult.

questions.question: How does the passage connect this example to Divine creativity?
questions.answer: It says Allah’s creative action is unlimited, so reaching many is no harder than reaching one.

questions.question: Which two beings are mentioned as examples of something luminous?
questions.answer: An eye and Gabriel.

questions.question: What ability is described for a luminous being in this passage?
questions.answer: It can be present in, look into, or enter many places as easily as one place.

questions.question: What role does Divine mercy play in this explanation?
questions.answer: The passage says this wide-reaching activity happens within the manifestation of mercy.

questions.question: What repeated principle appears in both major examples of the passage?
questions.answer: The repeated principle is that multiplicity does not create difficulty for Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the phrase about no difference between many and few mean in simple words?
questions.answer: It means Allah is not limited like creation, so handling countless things is as easy as handling one.

questions.question: What truth about Allah’s power is the passage trying to make clear?
questions.answer: That Allah can act in many places and upon many things at once without strain or limitation.

questions.question: Why does the passage begin with examples from light and reflection?
questions.answer: Because they help the reader picture how one source can appear in many places at the same time.

questions.question: In the first comparison, what allows one sun to appear in countless places?
questions.answer: Its light can be reflected by many surfaces.

questions.question: Besides light, what two other effects of the sun are mentioned as reaching many reflectors?
questions.answer: Its warmth and its reflected image.

questions.question: What is meant by saying that large and small are alike in this context?
questions.answer: It means size does not make something easier or harder for Divine power.

questions.question: How does the example of speech support the same lesson?
questions.answer: One statement can be heard by one listener or many listeners without changing the statement itself.

questions.question: What does this suggest about the range of Allah’s creating activity?
questions.answer: It suggests His activity is vast and unrestricted.

questions.question: Why is Gabriel mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: He is used as an example of a luminous spirit being that can be related to many places at once by Allah’s power.

questions.question: What three actions are said to be possible for such a being in many places?
questions.answer: Being present, seeing, and entering.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes this wide presence possible?
questions.answer: Divine power and Allah’s permission.

questions.question: Which matters are said to be equal in difficulty for Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: One and many, and also great and small.

questions.question: Why are ordinary examples like mirrors and hearing useful in this passage?
questions.answer: They make a deep belief easier to understand by connecting it to familiar experiences.

questions.question: State the central lesson of the whole passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: Allah’s command and power reach countless things at once with the same ease as reaching a single thing.

questions.question: What is being explained under the title “Second Mystery”?
questions.answer: A reason why Allah’s power is not burdened by multiplicity, size, or number.

questions.question: What natural object is the first teaching example in the passage?
questions.answer: The sun.

questions.question: How is the sun used as a comparison rather than as the main subject?
questions.answer: Its reflections are used to help explain, by analogy, how one source can relate to many recipients.

questions.question: What kinds of recipients of the sun’s reflection are listed?
questions.answer: Mirrors, bright surfaces, and drops of water.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the difference between one reflector and many reflectors?
questions.answer: It says the difference does not create difficulty in receiving the reflection.

questions.question: What human experience is used as the next comparison?
questions.answer: Hearing a spoken word.

questions.question: How does one spoken word support the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: The same word can reach one ear or many ears, showing that one act can spread widely.

questions.question: What phrase shows that Allah’s creative activity is not limited?
questions.answer: The passage describes it as having unlimited breadth.

questions.question: Which examples in the passage involve living or spiritual beings rather than objects?
questions.answer: The eye and Gabriel.

questions.question: What do these examples add to the earlier examples of sunlight and speech?
questions.answer: They show that wide presence or contact is not only an idea about objects but also about living and spiritual realities by Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about space and place in relation to Divine power?
questions.answer: Being in many places is not difficult for what Allah enables through His power.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the line that many and few are the same?
questions.answer: Number does not weaken or divide Allah’s ability.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the logic of the passage?
questions.answer: If created examples can show one source reaching many places, then Allah’s unlimited power can certainly act upon countless things with complete ease.

questions.question: What key belief is supported by the examples in this passage?
questions.answer: The belief that Allah’s power is unlimited and not made difficult by dealing with many things.

questions.question: What three words at the start point to the reason the examples work?
questions.answer: They point to brightness, clearness, and submission.

questions.question: In the first example, what remains the same whether there is one mirror or many?
questions.answer: The source remains one while its effects appear in many places.

questions.question: Why is the mention of heat important in the sun comparison?
questions.answer: It shows that not only appearance but also effect can spread widely from one source.

questions.question: What lesson comes from comparing one listener with a million listeners?
questions.answer: Reaching many does not necessarily make an action harder.

questions.question: How does the passage move from physical examples to spiritual ones?
questions.answer: It starts with sunlight, then speech, and then mentions the eye and an angelic being.

questions.question: What does this progression help the reader do?
questions.answer: It helps the reader move from simple visible examples to deeper unseen realities.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is needed for such broad activity to happen?
questions.answer: Divine command, Divine power, and Allah’s permission.

questions.question: What is suggested by saying that Gabriel may attend many places as easily as one?
questions.answer: It suggests that Allah can enable a being to act beyond normal human limits.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge the human habit of measuring ability by quantity?
questions.answer: It teaches that for Allah, quantity does not create the limits it creates for us.

questions.question: What contrast between human action and Divine action can be inferred here?
questions.answer: Humans get overwhelmed by larger numbers, but Allah does not.

questions.question: What is the function of repeated statements that there is no difference?
questions.answer: They emphasize the main point so the reader clearly understands it.

questions.question: Why are both “great and small” and “many and few” mentioned?
questions.answer: To show that neither size nor number affects Allah’s power.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is mainly used in this passage: storytelling, command, or analogy?
questions.answer: Analogy.

questions.question: Give a short faith-centered takeaway from this passage.
questions.answer: A believer should trust that Allah’s power fully covers all things, whether they are few or countless.

questions.question: What is the passage trying to prove through examples?
questions.answer: That one Divine act can reach countless things with complete ease.

questions.question: What feature of the sun makes it a useful comparison here?
questions.answer: Its light can appear in many reflecting places from one source.

questions.question: What is the meaning of “boundless creativity” in the example of the spoken word?
questions.answer: It means Allah’s creating is not restricted or narrowed by numbers.

questions.question: Why is a spoken word a strong example for this argument?
questions.answer: Because the same message can be received by many people without being split up or weakened.

questions.question: What does the passage say a luminous being can do in relation to many places?
questions.answer: It can be present in them, observe them, or enter them.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both an eye and Gabriel?
questions.answer: To give examples from different levels of created beings that help illustrate the same point.

questions.question: What does “with dominical permission” add to the meaning of the example?
questions.answer: It shows that such ability exists only by Allah’s allowing and ruling.

questions.question: What repeated pattern do all the examples share?
questions.answer: In each case, one source relates to many receivers without added difficulty.

questions.question: What does this passage teach about Allah’s relationship to quantity?
questions.answer: Quantity does not burden or limit Him.

questions.question: What can a student infer about the purpose of these comparisons?
questions.answer: Their purpose is to bring a hard-to-grasp belief closer to understanding.

questions.question: Write the message of the passage in simple everyday words.
questions.answer: Allah can handle everything, no matter how many there are, just as easily as handling one thing.

questions.question: Under the “Second Mystery,” what problem or question is being addressed?
questions.answer: How it can be easy for Allah to deal with countless beings at the same time.

questions.question: What is the first sign from the created world used to answer that question?
questions.answer: The way one sun is reflected in many places.

questions.question: What are the receiving objects in that first sign meant to show?
questions.answer: They show how many things can receive from one source at once.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from the reflection example?
questions.answer: That multiplicity does not necessarily create difficulty.

questions.question: What is the second comparison taken from ordinary life?
questions.answer: One statement being heard by one person or by a huge crowd.

questions.question: Why is hearing used as a comparison?
questions.answer: Because it is easy to imagine one sound reaching many listeners together.

questions.question: What does the phrase about unlimited creative breadth teach about Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that His activity has no narrow limits.

questions.question: Which examples in the passage point beyond the physical world?
questions.answer: The mention of a spiritual being like Gabriel and the ability to be connected with many places.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the difficulty of entering one place versus many places for such a being?
questions.answer: It says there is no difference when Allah enables it.

questions.question: How are permission and power connected in this passage?
questions.answer: Broad action happens by Allah’s permission and through His power.

questions.question: What two pairs are directly treated as equal in difficulty?
questions.answer: Big and small, and many and few.

questions.question: What belief about Allah becomes stronger if this passage is accepted?
questions.answer: Belief that Allah’s control and command cover all creation perfectly.

questions.question: Why does the passage use several examples instead of just one?
questions.answer: Multiple examples reinforce the idea from different angles and make it easier to grasp.

questions.question: What misunderstanding about Divine power does this passage correct?
questions.answer: It corrects the idea that dealing with many things must be harder than dealing with one.

questions.question: What is one respectful personal lesson a Muslim student can take from this passage?
questions.answer: We should not doubt Allah’s ability because of the greatness or number of created things, since all are equally easy for Him.
